beats.html:
The rule of thumb
Under $1M in revenue? Probably don't buy a business.

The rule of thumb
Over $1M? It might be the best thing you ever do.

Think like the bank
What kind of business does a bank want to finance?

What banks want
1Not a bad business
2A profitable business
3A lot of profit, not $50k or $100k

Remember this
It's easier to borrow $100M than $1M.

Why
1Bankers have quotas
2Targets every quarter
3A bonus for hitting them

The banker mentality
Multi-million deals hit the target.

Remember this
Larger amounts are easier to borrow than small ones.

Under $1M
You're probably still working in the business.

Over $1M
1A system and a foundation
2Staff, not just you
3Hiring, training, day-to-day protocols

What the banker sees
Less risk. Easier to lend against.

Raising money for a deal
How are you removing the risk?

How Josh teaches it
Answer the bank's questions before they ask.

Present everything upfront
So the only question left is how much?

How most people do it
"Please, how much can you give me?"
That's not how money works in the corporate world.

Ask like that, and they want
1Your personal guarantee
2Your personal assets and home
3Your business as collateral

Josh's view
Corporate lending is highly unregulated.

With deals
1Not the retail route
2The corporate route
3Better still: your industry's team

In Australia
The big banks have industry divisions.
Josh only talks to healthcare bankers.

In short
1Little business: a lot of risk
2Big business: less risk
3Big money is easier to get
It's a matter of presenting it properly.

Under a million?
Build a business that runs without you.

The test
If you dropped dead today, would it still make money?

Begin with the end in mind
Build it to sell one day.

Josh's strategy
1Buy
2Optimise
3Flip

Act as if
Act as if. Make it happen.

Even his first business
Structured like a sellable asset.

The trade-off
Hiring people bit into his margins.

Why pick an industry you don't know
1Less likely to overthink
2More likely to take action

Certainty is a trap
The people who make leaps just jump.

Under a million right now?
1Under $500k: don't buy a business
2$500k–$1M: only if it runs without you

Ask yourself
When something goes wrong, who handles it?

Real life
Often stranger than fiction.

On planning
Plan, but expect the plan to change on day one.

Today's question
Under $1M, over $1M: to buy or not to buy.
